newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Telstra sees faster Internet growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Telstra sees faster Internet growth.

text.p: Australian government owned Telstra Corp said on Thursday it now expected total international Internet traffic to exceed international telephone, data and video traffic by the last quarter of 1998, not the turn of the century as earlier predicted.
Telstra chief executive Frank Blount told a business luncheon the Internet had emerged quickly, posing both threat and opportunity to carriers like Telstra.
Now used by 1.1 million Australians, the emergence of the Internet proved Telstra had made the right decision in rolling out a new cable network, he said.
"The Internet has grown faster than we had ever anticipated, but we were pointing in the right direction to capture its potential and to build on it," he said.

Speaking of Telstra's focus to grow its established core market, Blount said benchmark analysis showed Telstra was around 25 percent to 30 percent off current best practice, measured by operating expenses per access line.

It had already achieved an annual underlying productivity improvement of 10-12 percent, principally through technological investment, but that rate "must accelerate fairly dramatically very quickly", he said.
Blount said the proposed listing on the Australian Stock Exchange of one-third of Telxtra would take place "arguably in the next several months or maybe early next year".
